chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from some of our companions, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said:

"If a man fears for his self, he delays his ihram until al-Haram." And whoever's residence is below (shorter distance than) these miqats that we have mentioned, then his miqat is his residence, and he is obliged to enter into ihram from it. He narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.مِيقَاتٌ: Designated station/place where pilgrims enter ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the miqat for someone living closer to Mecca than the standard stations?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal principle that for residents of Mecca (Ahl al-Haram), their home serves as their miqat, distinguishing them from travelers who must stop at designated stations. It further introduces the concession of delaying ihram until entering the sacred precincts if one fears for their safety, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) in ritual obligations. This ruling underscores the unique status of Mecca's inhabitants in Hajj jurisprudence, as recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi.
